thread:
elaine: heads up — since yesterday we've seen intermittent CI runner failures in the linux-build pool. root cause looks like 'impersonation window expired' when the runner tries to get an ephemeral token to impersonate the deploy SA. started ~04:10 UTC, affects ~25% of jobs. logs attached below.

ajay: can you paste the exact error and the command the runner is using to fetch the token? are we running the new token-broker change?

elaine: error from runner logs: `ERROR: token fetch failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = impersonation window expired (requested at 2024-11-12T04:10:12Z)`
config excerpt from the runner job:
```
env:
  - SA_IMPERSONATE=ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  - TOKEN_EXP=3600
command:
  gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=$SA_IMPERSONATE --audiences=https://redwood-inference/api
```

matthew: we rolled the tighter impersonation window last week (reducing allowed skew for cached impersonations to 30s) to harden sessions. didn't expect churn for long-running pipeline tasks.

ci-sre-bot: ALERT: 24 failed jobs in linux-build in last 1h (impersonation-window). See: https://grafana.internal/alert/ci-impersonation-window

ops-bot: quick workaround — set TOKEN_EXP to 900 and force runners to request fresh tokens immediately before heavy steps, or revert the impersonation skew to 5m until we patch.

ajay: repro steps I used:
1) run local repro with service account A impersonating B:
```bash
# request identity token with impersonation
gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --audiences=ci-runner
# run immediately then sleep >35s then re-run step that reuses cached token
```
observed the same "impersonation window expired" after ~32s of delay.

ajay: immediate remediation options:
- grant the CI runner service account roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA with condition limiting to the job name (least-privilege).
- increase impersonation cache window on token-broker to 300s for the linux-build pool only.
- migrate runners to generate fully ephemeral tokens per-step via OIDC (preferred long-term).

matthew: config snippet for least-privilege binding (Terraform):
```hcl
resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "ci_impersonate" {
  service_account_id = "projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/ci-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  role               = "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
  members            = ["serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
  condition {
    title       = "ci-job-bound"
    expression  = "request.auth.claims.job == \"linux-build\""
  }
}
```

ops-bot: If you want to test the OIDC-based short-lived tokens locally:
```bash
# example: request an access token via workload identity federation (no SA key)
gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=ci-runner --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
This will avoid relying on cached impersonation state.

elaine: verified that bumping the runner to request fresh tokens before the deploy step reduces failures to ~2% (probably unrelated flaky infra). rolling this change as a stopgap now. will open a PR to add the TF role binding snippet to infra repo.

support: tagging infra-oncall and security for visibility — possible impact on least-privilege posture if we temporarily relax the window. @ajay can you open the infra ticket with repro steps + logs?

ajay: filing ticket now with: repro commands, sample logs, suggestion to add conditional iam binding + long-term OIDC migration plan. attaching the terraform snippet and recommended rollout (canary pool => full).

matthew: ack. follow-up: let's run a 24h canary with increased token freshness and monitor error rate in Grafana. also check for any billing anomalies due to extra token requests (should be negligible).

elaine: thanks — I'll update the pipeline template and ping when canary starts. :thumbsup:
